questionBankSnapshot.action: No bulk question generation or rewriting; strengthen response, troubleshooting, documentation, and escalation routing.

policy: Use one reasoning scaffold across D2C: recognize -> verify patient and signal -> document -> permitted technical correction -> escalate per facility policy. Current AASM scoring/technical authority controls rule-sensitive signal interpretation; AAST current technical, competency, scope, and role sources guide technologist workflow; physician orders, facility SOPs, state/scope requirements, and manufacturer instructions control local execution.

responseSequence.label: Recognize
responseSequence.instruction: Identify the observed pattern, signal problem, treatment change, or safety concern without assuming the cause.

responseSequence.label: Verify patient and signal
responseSequence.instruction: Check the patient and corroborating physiologic channels, then verify relevant sensors, connections, calibration, and device context before deciding artifact versus physiology.

responseSequence.label: Document
responseSequence.instruction: Record the observation, timing, relevant patient/signal verification, and context before or during intervention as local workflow permits.

responseSequence.label: Permitted technical correction
responseSequence.instruction: Perform only corrections allowed by current technical guidance, role/scope, orders, facility procedure, and manufacturer instructions; then reassess and document response.

responseSequence.label: Escalate per facility policy
responseSequence.instruction: Escalate unresolved abnormalities, patient-safety concerns, clinical decisions, or actions outside technologist scope through the facility-defined chain.

safetyOverride: The sequence is a reasoning scaffold, not a reason to delay urgent patient-safety action. If an immediate threat is apparent, activate the facility emergency response while continuing verification and documentation as feasible.

routes.label: Adult PSG signal artifact and recording-quality response
routes.boundary: For adult standard PSG, verify the patient and physiologic cross-correlation before correcting the signal. AAST Standard PSG is not pediatric, HSAT, PAP, or oxygen authority.

routes.label: Possible physiologic or patient-safety event
routes.boundary: A potentially real physiologic event is not merely an artifact problem. Verify the patient and corroborating signals, document, and use the local escalation/emergency pathway for clinical decisions or safety threats.

routes.label: Airflow, effort, oximetry, and respiratory-signal disagreement
routes.boundary: Do not classify a respiratory event from a single failed channel. Cross-check patient, airflow, effort, oximetry, position, and signal integrity as applicable; pediatric cases route through the pediatric/infant crosswalk rather than adult Standard PSG authority.

routes.label: ETCO2 and TcCO2 troubleshooting
routes.boundary: Keep ETCO2 and TcCO2 distinct. Verify calibration, waveform/trend, sensor behavior, patient context, and corroborating signals. Oximetry is not a substitute for ventilation assessment.

routes.label: Cardiac rhythm recognition, verification, and escalation
routes.boundary: Teach recognition, signal verification, technical documentation, and facility escalation. Do not convert rhythm recognition into independent diagnosis, medication advice, or a universal emergency threshold.

routes.label: Treatment-related respiratory or device change
routes.boundary: Route the response back to the treatment indication and modality. Do not improvise PAP, ASV, NIV, oxygen, or other treatment settings outside the applicable order, current guidance, facility protocol, and manufacturer instructions.

routes.label: Pediatric and infant response boundary
routes.boundary: Use current AASM pediatric/infant rules and age-specific competency. AAST Standard PSG must not be presented as pediatric PSG authority; local caregiver, safety, and escalation procedures remain facility-specific.

routes.label: Equipment, maintenance, cleaning, and safety response
routes.boundary: Use facility procedures and manufacturer instructions for device-specific maintenance, cleaning, electrical/safety response, and replacement decisions rather than memorizing a universal repair sequence.

routes.label: Technical documentation and escalation handoff
routes.boundary: Document what was observed, patient/signal verification, technical action, reassessment/response, and escalation according to local workflow. Documentation should support physician interpretation without implying the technologist independently diagnosed or prescribed treatment.

explicitNonRules: No universal heart-rate, SpO2, blood-pressure, arrhythmia, seizure, respiratory, or other emergency threshold is hard-coded for every sleep laboratory.
No universal who-to-call sequence replaces the facility emergency/escalation chain.
Do not repair or suppress a signal before checking whether the patient may be experiencing a real physiologic event.
Do not treat a single abnormal channel as proof of physiology without corroboration when signal failure is plausible.
Do not make treatment changes beyond the applicable order, current guidance, scope, facility procedure, and manufacturer instructions.
Do not let documentation requirements delay immediate facility emergency response when a clear patient-safety threat is present.

remainingGaps.topic: Facility-specific emergency thresholds, escalation chain, standing orders, and device repair limits
remainingGaps.handling: Teach the verification and escalation framework; require the learner to use the facility policy/order/manufacturer layer for exact local actions.
